title: The Evening Prayer: Wagner's Copyist, His Sister's Four Songs, and the Opera That Ate a Name
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Siegburg, the schoolmaster's house on the Markt
stops.date_confidence: attested; the house is identified as Markt 46, the town Gymnasium built from 1826, now the Stadtmuseum Siegburg, per the German Wikipedia article on that museum
stops.campa: On the first of September a son is born to Gustav Humperdinck, a teacher at the Siegburg Gymnasium, and to Gertrud, a cantor's daughter, in the building on the Markt where the school itself is housed. They name him Engelbert. The house has stood since 1826 and will outlast him; a century and a half later it holds the city's museum, and the room of his birth is a room the public walks through. The Rhine Province is Prussian, the town is small, and the father who teaches in the rooms below intends his son for a profession with a drawing board in it.
suggested_refs: Markt 46, Siegburg: the former town Gymnasium, birth house, now Stadtmuseum Siegburg

stops.name: Siegburg, the parish church of Saint Servatius
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; local civic tradition only, no parish register consulted for this file, and the day is assumed from the birth date
stops.campa: Tradition carries the infant a few hundred paces uphill to Saint Servatius, the parish church of the town, for baptism. No parish register has been consulted, and the ceremony is reconstruction rather than record. Above the town on its own hill stands the Benedictine abbey of Saint Michael, a different house entirely and the one usually meant when Siegburg and Benedictines are named in the same sentence. The boy will spend his working life putting sacred furniture on secular stages: an evening prayer for two lost children, and angels counted out fourteen at a time.
suggested_refs: St. Servatius, Siegburg: Propsteikirche, distinct from the Abtei Michaelsberg above the town
sources: Siegburg civic tradition, unverified against parish records

stops.name: Siegburg, two singspiele at thirteen
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; the anecdotes are undated in the source and the years here are arithmetic performed on the phrases 'about seven' and 'about thirteen'
stops.campa: The childhood anecdotes come down without dates. He is given piano lessons and writes something of his own at about seven; at about thirteen he sets two singspiele for the stage. His parents are not pleased by any of it. They want architecture for him, a trade with drawings and measurements and a salary, and English Wikipedia is explicit that they discouraged the music. He goes on writing. Nothing of these first pieces survives in any source consulted, and the years assigned to them here are inference, not documents.
suggested_refs: The undated childhood anecdotes in the English Wikipedia article, source of both the age-seven piece and the two singspiele

stops.name: Paderborn, the Gymnasium Theodorianum
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by German Wikipedia; month and day not given
stops.campa: He takes his Abitur at the Gymnasium Theodorianum in Paderborn, a school old enough to have been founded in the eighth century. Westphalia is not the Rhineland; the Latin is the same. He leaves it qualified for a university and for the respectable career his family has in view, and goes back to the Rhine to begin a building apprenticeship, a Baulehre with a drawing office at the end of it. The apprenticeship lasts months. What ends it is a decision no source records in his own words; the German article says only that he broke it off.
suggested_refs: Gymnasium Theodorianum, Paderborn, and its 1871 Abitur registers

stops.name: Cologne, the conservatory of Ferdinand Hiller
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by both Wikipedias; the aborted architecture apprenticeship belongs to 1871 and the conservatory enrolment to 1872, and the two must not be collapsed into one year
stops.campa: The drawing office is abandoned and he enrols at the Cologne Conservatory, composition under Ferdinand Hiller, piano under Isidor Seiss. One account credits his mother with backing the change; English Wikipedia says the opposite, that his parents pushed him toward architecture. The two accounts do not agree, and neither is settled here. He is eighteen, in a city of Romanesque churches far older than the conservatory itself, among them the ninth-century monastery church of Saint Pantaleon, a survival from an age long before Cologne had a school of music at all.
suggested_refs: The Kölner Konservatorium under Ferdinand Hiller, and Isidor Seiss's piano class

stops.name: Cologne, the Mozart Prize out of Frankfurt
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by German Wikipedia; month and day not given
stops.campa: The Mozart Prize, awarded from Frankfurt, comes to him and the money ends a stretch of real hardship. Prizes will move him across Europe for the next four years the way commissions move other men: this one keeps him at his desk, the next carries him to Munich, the third to Italy and to the door of a villa where Richard Wagner is spending the winter. He is twenty-two. He has written nothing that anyone outside a conservatory has heard, and he will not write it for another seventeen years.
suggested_refs: The Frankfurt Mozart-Stiftung prize of 1876

segments.name: Munich, and the Money to Travel

stops.name: Munich, the Odeon and the Royal Music School
stops.date_confidence: contested year: German Wikipedia gives 1877, English Wikipedia gives 1876; the German date is used for sequence and the disagreement is not resolved. The coordinate is the Odeon on Odeonsplatz, which housed the Koenigliche Musikschule
stops.campa: On a scholarship he moves to Munich and enters the Royal Music School, housed in the Odeon on the Odeonsplatz, to study with Franz Lachner and with Josef Rheinberger. Lachner belongs to Schubert's Vienna and remembers it; Rheinberger teaches counterpoint as a moral discipline. Munich in the 1870s is the city where Wagner's operas were first heard and where Wagner is no longer welcome. Humperdinck learns the older craft thoroughly here, and it is the older craft that will carry the fairy-tale opera when he finally writes one.
suggested_refs: The Odeon, Odeonsplatz, Munich: home of the Koenigliche Musikschule under Rheinberger

stops.name: Berlin, the Mendelssohn Foundation prize
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by both Wikipedias; the award site within Berlin is not recorded and the coordinate is a city-centre approximation
stops.campa: The Mendelssohn Foundation in Berlin gives him its prize, a scholarship endowed by the composer's family and meant to be spent abroad. Where in Berlin the award is made is not recorded in any source reachable here; the coordinate is the city centre and admits as much. What the money buys is a year and more of Italy, France and Spain, out of which the record preserves two or three named places and loses the rest. He completes his Munich studies in the same year and leaves Germany with a purse and no post.
suggested_refs: The Mendelssohn-Stiftung travelling scholarship, awarded 1879

stops.name: Rome, a station on the scholar's road
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; no source consulted places Humperdinck in Rome on any day. English Wikipedia says only that he travelled through Italy, France and Spain, and Rome is supplied here from the conventional itinerary of a German scholarship-holder
stops.campa: English Wikipedia says he travelled through Italy, France and Spain, and names no city. Rome is the traditional first station of a German scholarship-holder going south, and it stands here on that tradition alone. The stop is kept because the road is real and the route is lost, and marking the loss is better than inventing a line across a map. The next place the record can actually see him is a villa on a headland above the bay of Naples, and between Berlin and that villa the sources hold nothing but the names of three countries.
suggested_refs: The standard Italian itinerary of nineteenth-century German prize scholars, against which this gap should be read
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Engelbert Humperdinck (composer)': 'travelled through Italy, France, and Spain'

stops.name: Naples, the Villa Angri on Posillipo
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by both Wikipedias; day not given. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the canonical Naples pin in richard_wagner.journey.json
stops.campa: The Wagner family is wintering at the Villa Angri on the Posillipo slope above the Bay of Naples, where Richard Wagner is at work on the last act of Parsifal. Humperdinck, twenty-five and travelling on Mendelssohn money, presents himself at the door and is received. The meeting decides the next decade of his life. He enters a household that treats its master as a religion treats a founder, and his own composing stops, and stays stopped for years while he learns to serve another man's score instead of writing his own.
suggested_refs: Villa Doria d'Angri, Posillipo: the Wagner family's winter residence, 1880
sources: richard_wagner.journey.json, stop 'Naples, the Villa Angri and Klingsor's garden'

stops.name: Bayreuth, the house called Wahnfried
stops.date_confidence: attested; German Wikipedia dates the Bayreuth assistantship from January 1881 to July 1882. The coordinate is Wahnfried itself, where he worked; the sources do not say he lodged in the house
stops.campa: He comes to Bayreuth in January and works at Wahnfried as Wagner's assistant, copying and correcting the score of Parsifal and tutoring the household's son Siegfried, who is eleven. The sources say he worked there; they do not say he lived there, and the difference is not stretched here. He is inside the workshop where Wagner's last opera is being finished, and the work he does there is a copyist's. Of his own production in these years he later writes that it came to a sudden end.
stops.quote: Seitdem ich zu Wagner nach Bayreuth gekommen bin, hat es mit der eigenen Produktion ein plötzliches Ende genommen. ... Die Hauptsache ist, dass ich mich selbst wieder finde, nachdem ich mir nun Jahre entfremdet gewesen.
stops.quote_source: Humperdinck, letter to a friend, quoted in the German Wikipedia article 'Engelbert Humperdinck', citing Wolfram Humperdinck, 'Engelbert Humperdinck: Das Leben meines Vaters' (1965); recipient and exact date not given in the source consulted
suggested_refs: Haus Wahnfried, Bayreuth, and the Parsifal copyists' work of 1881-1882

stops.name: Bayreuth, the bar of trombone in Parsifal
stops.date_confidence: attested for the premiere date; the anecdote of the interpolated bars is Wagner-Bayreuth historiography rather than a documented act, and is carried as tradition. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the canonical Bayreuth Festspielhaus pin in richard_wagner.journey.json
stops.campa: Parsifal has its premiere on the Green Hill, and behind the scenery a transformation runs longer than the music written to cover it. Humperdinck writes the extra bars himself, and the interpolation is found out and, the story goes, tolerated. It is the single measure of his hand inside Wagner's score, added at the workbench and smoothed over rather than credited. He stands at the scene dock through the performance, watching the machinery he helped build keep pace with a work he has spent a year and a half copying out by hand.
suggested_refs: Ernest Newman, 'The Life of Richard Wagner', on the Parsifal transformation-music problem of 1882
sources: Ernest Newman, 'The Life of Richard Wagner'

stops.name: Venice, the death of Wagner
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by German Wikipedia; the Venetian coordinate is the Palazzo Vendramin-Calergi, standard in the Wagner literature and not separately verified for this file
stops.campa: Wagner dies at Venice, six months after the last Parsifal of the first season and seven after the assistantship ended. The German article states plainly that the death affects Humperdinck deeply, and gives no more than that. He is twenty-eight and without a post. The household that had supplied him with both a trade and a manner is finished. What follows is a decade of taking whatever work is offered, in three countries, and of publishing almost nothing over his own name.
suggested_refs: Palazzo Vendramin-Calergi, Venice, where Wagner died on 13 February 1883

stops.name: Southern Europe, the years the sources do not record
stops.date_confidence: explicit gap; the sources describe an undated span running from roughly 1881 to 1885 with no dates and no cities. The date here is a placeholder holding the stop's place in sequence, and the coordinate is the geometric middle of the Italian peninsula, marking an absence rather than a place
stops.campa: Beyond Naples and a passing mention of Palermo, the surviving sources describe his travels through Italy, France and Spain only in general terms. No city is named and no letter is quoted. This gap is left in place so that the hole is counted rather than filled, because several years of an otherwise documented life reduce here to the names of three countries and a scholarship that paid for them. What is known about this stretch is only that it happened, and that he came back north.
suggested_refs: The unrecorded 1880s itinerary: an explicit gap, flagged for future archival work
sources: English Wikipedia, 'Engelbert Humperdinck (composer)': 'travelled through Italy, France, and Spain'

stops.name: Cologne, the Stadttheater and the dismissal
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; German Wikipedia gives the post and the dismissal without precise dates, the geography lens of the research pool offers only a 1883-1885 span, and the date here is a placeholder inside that span. The theatre coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: Back in the Rhineland he takes a Kapellmeister's post at the Cologne city theatre and loses it. The German article records the dismissal without the cause and without the span of the appointment. In these same years he is engaged as a musical companion attached to the household of the steel manufacturer Alfred Krupp, work of the kind that keeps a musician fed and leaves no scores behind it. He is thirty. A Wagner apprenticeship stands on his record, and there is no career under it.
suggested_refs: The Koelner Stadttheater engagement, undated in the sources, and the 1885 Krupp appointment

stops.name: Barcelona, the conservatory of the Liceu
stops.date_confidence: contested duration: German Wikipedia gives autumn 1885 to summer 1886, under a year; English Wikipedia says roughly two years, which cannot be fitted to a summer 1886 return. The German span is used and the English figure is not silently discarded
stops.campa: He crosses to Spain to teach composition at the conservatory attached to the Gran Teatre del Liceu on the Rambla. German Wikipedia gives the stay as autumn 1885 to the summer of 1886; the English article says roughly two years, which cannot be squared with a return in the summer of 1886, and the two stand against each other here without a verdict. Barcelona is the furthest from the Rhine he will ever live. What he composed there, if he composed, does not reach any consulted source.
suggested_refs: The conservatory attached to the Gran Teatre del Liceu, Barcelona, and its teaching rolls for 1885-1886

stops.name: Cologne, the return from Spain
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by English Wikipedia; the conservatory post is left in 1888 per German Wikipedia, with no month given in either article
stops.campa: He comes back to Cologne and to the conservatory that had trained him, holding a post there until 1888. English Wikipedia dates the return to 1887 and attaches to it a period of work as a music critic; the German article puts the criticism in a different city on a different paper, and the two are kept apart here rather than folded together. He is thirty-three, a returned professor of nothing in particular. Hänsel und Gretel is six years off, and nothing on the record so far predicts it.
suggested_refs: The Koelner Konservatorium appointment of 1887-1888, left in 1888 with no month recorded

stops.name: Bonn, the notices in the Bonner Zeitung
stops.date_confidence: attested by German Wikipedia as to paper and city, undated as to span; the English article places a critic's post at Cologne instead, and the two are not reconciled by any source consulted
stops.campa: German Wikipedia has him writing music criticism for the Bonner Zeitung, upriver from Cologne. English Wikipedia has him a critic too, but in Cologne; the papers differ and the cities differ, and no source consulted brings them together. He is judging other men's operas in print in the years before he writes one himself. Five years from now he will be married in Poppelsdorf, a Bonn suburb within an easy walk of wherever this newspaper kept its offices, and by then the notices will be about him.
suggested_refs: The Bonner Zeitung of the late 1880s: Humperdinck's signed and unsigned music criticism, unindexed

stops.name: Mainz, the house of B. Schott's Söhne
stops.date_confidence: attested as to employment by German Wikipedia; the 1887-1889 span is approximate and no month is given. The coordinate is the firm's premises at Weihergarten 5
stops.campa: At the Weihergarten in Mainz he works as an editor for B. Schott's Söhne, preparing scores for the press, among them piano reductions of Wagner. He leaves the Cologne conservatory post in the same year, in a month no source reachable here supplies. Editing is the trade that teaches a composer how a page must look to a singer and to a répétiteur at a rehearsal piano. Two years of it, then Frankfurt, and then a letter from his sister asking for four songs for the children to sing at home.
suggested_refs: B. Schott's Söhne, Weihergarten 5, Mainz: house editing records of the late 1880s
sources: New Grove, 'Humperdinck, Engelbert' (not re-consulted in this session)

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, Dr. Hoch's Konservatorium
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by both Wikipedias; no month given. The coordinate is Eschersheimer Landstraße 4, the institution's address, not the city centre
stops.campa: He is appointed to teach at Dr. Hoch's Conservatory on the Eschersheimer Landstraße, takes harmony at the Stockhausen vocal school besides, and is engaged by the Frankfurter Zeitung as its opera critic. At thirty-six it is his first settled professional footing, salaried and respectable. He has by now spent eighteen years inside music schools as pupil and as teacher. The work that will carry his name out of Germany is begun in this city in the same year, at a domestic request, for a performance in a family drawing room.
stops.quote_source: Humperdinck's own genre label for 'Hänsel und Gretel', recorded in the English Wikipedia article 'Hansel and Gretel (opera)'; the coinage is attributed to him there without citation of a letter or interview
suggested_refs: Dr. Hoch's Konservatorium, Eschersheimer Landstraße 4, Frankfurt, and its teaching rolls from 1890

stops.name: Frankfurt am Main, the songs his sister asked for
stops.date_confidence: attested for the 1891-1892 composition span; the address Scheffelstraße 1 appears in one lens of the research pool and is absent from the Wikipedia articles as fetched, so the street coordinate in the Nordend is used and the address itself is flagged as unsourced
stops.campa: Adelheid Wette asks her brother to set songs for a children's play she has made out of the Grimm tale of Hänsel und Gretel; the songs grow into an opera, written here across 1891 and 1892. One lens of the research gives the address as Scheffelstraße 1 in the Nordend and another says the residence is unidentified, and the contradiction is left standing rather than split. The tale itself reached the Grimms at Kassel from Dortchen Wild in the pharmacy on the Marktgasse.
stops.quote: Vergangenen Sonntag habe ich auch die Ouvertüre niedergeschrieben, die ein ziemlich ausgedehntes Musikstück geworden ist, eine Art symphonischer Prolog, der ein 'Kinderleben' genannt werden könnte. Er beginnt mit dem Schutzengelchoral, von Hörnern vorgetragen, geht dann über in das 'Hokus pokus', welches wiederum der Melodie 'Die Englein haben's uns im Traum gesagt' weichen muss, woran sich nun lustig 'Die Hexerei ist nun vorbei' in fröhlichem E-Dur anschließt.
stops.quote_source: Letter from Engelbert Humperdinck to his brother-in-law Hermann Wette, 16 December 1891, quoted in German in the German Wikipedia article 'Hänsel und Gretel (Oper)', section Musik; not cross-checked against an archival scan
suggested_refs: Scheffelstraße 1, Frankfurt-Nordend: the composition address, flagged as unsourced in the articles fetched
sources: brothers_grimm.journey.json, stop 'Kassel, the Wild pharmacy on the Marktgasse'

stops.name: Poppelsdorf bei Bonn, the marriage to Hedwig Taxer
stops.date_confidence: contested day: English Wikipedia gives 19 May 1892, German Wikipedia gives 18 May 1892. The month is recorded and the day is refused; the date field defaults to the first of the month rather than picking a side
stops.campa: He marries Hedwig Taxer, daughter of the bookseller Robert Taxer, at Poppelsdorf near Bonn. English Wikipedia dates the wedding to the nineteenth of May and German Wikipedia to the eighteenth, so the month stands and the day is left open. Four children will follow, among them Wolfram, who is going to write his father's life and, when the father's hand fails, hold the pen for him. The opera is finished or nearly finished as they marry, and neither of them yet knows what it is going to do to the household.
suggested_refs: The Poppelsdorf marriage register for May 1892, which would settle the 18th against the 19th

stops.name: Weimar, the premiere under Richard Strauss
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day, cross-confirmed by both Wikipedias. Coordinate inherited byte-identical from the canonical Weimar pin in saint_barbara.journey.json
stops.campa: Two days before Christmas, Hänsel und Gretel is heard for the first time at the Grand Ducal Court Theatre in Weimar, conducted by Richard Strauss, and it succeeds at once and everywhere. The evening prayer of the fourteen angels, sung kneeling before the children sleep, leaves the theatre within weeks and goes into the country's nurseries, hummed by mothers who have never set foot in an opera house. Goethe's Weimar acquires a second musical date to stand beside its literary ones. Humperdinck is thirty-nine, and for the only time in his life a work of his own reaches every corner of the country at once.
stops.quote: the first German composer of distinct individuality since Wagner
stops.quote_source: Critic R. A. Streatfeild on Humperdinck, quoted in Henry Edward Krehbiel, 'The Mentor: Makers of Modern Opera', Vol. 1, No. 47 (Project Gutenberg ebook 49932)
suggested_refs: The Grossherzogliches Hoftheater, Weimar, now the Deutsches Nationaltheater: playbill of 23 December 1893
sources: saint_barbara.journey.json, stop 'Weimar, the fourteen angels of the evening prayer'

stops.name: London, Daly's Theatre and the English Hänsel
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by English Wikipedia. The coordinate marks the historic Cranbourn Street site of Daly's Theatre, which no longer stands
stops.campa: A year and three days after Weimar the opera reaches England, at Daly's Theatre by Leicester Square, in Constance Bache's translation, which becomes and stays the standard English text for generations of school halls and parish stages. The American premiere follows in New York in October 1895; the source consulted names no theatre for it, so no pin is set and the gap is left visible. The building at Cranbourn Street has long since gone. Bache's English words outlast the house that first spoke them.
suggested_refs: Constance Bache's English singing translation of Hänsel und Gretel, Daly's Theatre, 26 December 1894

stops.name: Munich, the melodrama of the king's children
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both Wikipedias. The 1894 commission is corrected here: English Wikipedia's article on Königskinder names Heinrich Porges, the playwright's father, as the man who asked for the music, not the playwright herself
stops.campa: Königskinder is heard first as a melodrama, spoken declamation notated in rhythm above an orchestra, at the Munich court opera. The commission came in 1894 from Heinrich Porges, whose daughter Else had written the play under the name Ernst Rosmer; she refused to let it be turned into an opera, which is exactly why her lines are spoken and not sung. She relents in 1907. The notation Humperdinck devises to pin pitchless speech to a bar line is studied afterward by composers who never mention his fairy tale.
suggested_refs: The 1897 Munich melodrama score of Königskinder and its Sprechgesang notation

stops.name: Boppard am Rhein, the little castle on the river
stops.date_confidence: no month is recorded for the Boppard purchase and the date here is placed for sequence only. Contested year for the professorship: English Wikipedia dates Wilhelm II's naming of him as professor to 1896, German Wikipedia ties the Boppard purchase to 1897. Both are kept; no month is given for either
stops.campa: He resigns the Frankfurt teaching and takes a villa above the Rhine at Boppard, the house the town still calls the Humperdinck-Schlösschen. Wilhelm II names him professor; the English article dates the title to 1896 and the German article ties the move here to 1897, and both years stand. He is forty-three, famous, and for the first time living on what he wrote rather than on what he taught. The river below his terrace is the one he was born beside, seventy kilometres upstream.
suggested_refs: The Humperdinck-Schlösschen at Boppard am Rhein

stops.name: Berlin, the master class at the Academy of Arts
stops.date_confidence: attested to the month by both Wikipedias, which agree on November 1900; no day is given
stops.campa: In November he moves to Berlin to head the master class in composition at the Royal Academy of Arts, a post he holds into 1920. Both Wikipedias agree on the month, a rare enough agreement between the two. He teaches through the empire's last decade and through its collapse, from the Meisterschule rooms, a man whose one famous work is about hunger in a forest. The students who pass through will find his idiom quaint, and several of them say so in print while he is alive to read it.
suggested_refs: The Meisterschule für musikalische Komposition, Königliche Akademie der Künste, Berlin, 1900-1920

stops.name: Berlin, the Court Opera and Die Heirat wider Willen
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by German Wikipedia
stops.campa: His comic opera Die Heirat wider Willen has its premiere at the Court Opera on Unter den Linden. It does not repeat Weimar. Nothing he writes after 1893 repeats Weimar, and he keeps writing anyway: further stage works, incidental music, choruses, a catalogue known chiefly to people who have gone looking for it on purpose. The house on Unter den Linden will play his fairy-tale opera at Christmas for a hundred years, and this one, on whose stage it stands tonight, almost never again.
suggested_refs: Die Heirat wider Willen, Königliche Hofoper Unter den Linden, 14 April 1905

stops.name: Berlin, Max Reinhardt's Shakespeare
stops.date_confidence: corrected and re-dated: the epoch-making Ein Sommernachtstraum opened in January 1905 at the Neues Theater am Schiffbauerdamm, before Reinhardt held the Deutsches Theater, which he leased in autumn 1905 and bought in 1906. This pin is the Deutsches Theater and this date is the later collaboration; the earlier venue is named rather than absorbed
stops.campa: He writes incidental music for Max Reinhardt, whose Shakespeare productions are remaking the German stage. The Midsummer Night's Dream that made Reinhardt's name opened in January 1905 at the Neues Theater am Schiffbauerdamm, before he held this house at all; the pin here is the Deutsches Theater and the date is the collaboration that followed his taking it over. Once more he scores fairies, and once more for another man's scenery, while his own forest is already in every German nursery.
suggested_refs: Reinhardt's Deutsches Theater Shakespeare cycle and Humperdinck's incidental scores

stops.name: New York, the Metropolitan and the sung Königskinder
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by both Wikipedias. The coordinate is the old Metropolitan Opera House at 1411 Broadway, corrected from a pin that sat two blocks north
stops.campa: Thirteen years after the spoken version, Königskinder is heard as a through-composed opera, and its world premiere is given not in Germany but at the Metropolitan Opera House on Thirty-ninth Street. The reception is triumphal. German Wikipedia reports the work being celebrated as the most important opera since Wagner's Parsifal, in the passive voice and without naming who said so, and no unattributed sentence is promoted here into any individual's verdict on him.
stops.quote: die wichtigste Oper seit Wagners Parsifal
stops.quote_source: German Wikipedia, 'Engelbert Humperdinck', on the reception of the Metropolitan premiere of 28 December 1910: 'Königskinder erntete triumphalen Beifall und wurde als „die wichtigste Oper seit Wagners Parsifal" gefeiert.' Passive construction; no speaker is named in the source
suggested_refs: Metropolitan Opera performance archive, Königskinder world premiere, 28 December 1910

stops.name: London, Das Mirakel and the illness
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by German Wikipedia for the London production; the hall is not named in the source and the coordinate is central London
stops.campa: His music for Das Mirakel, the wordless spectacle Reinhardt mounts in London, is heard two days before Christmas, eighteen years to the week after Weimar. During the visit he falls severely ill. The German article does not name the hall, so the coordinate here is central London and nothing finer. He is fifty-seven and has been a well man all his life, a professor with a country house and a standing Christmas repertory piece. Thirteen days later the illness acquires a date and a permanent consequence.
suggested_refs: Reinhardt's Das Mirakel, London, December 1911, with Humperdinck's score

stops.name: Berlin, the stroke of the fifth of January
stops.date_confidence: the date and the paralysis are attested by English Wikipedia, which names no city; German Wikipedia ties the collapse to the London journey without giving this day. Berlin is an inference from his residence and is not a source claim
stops.campa: A severe stroke leaves his left hand permanently paralysed. English Wikipedia supplies the date and the consequence and names no place; the German article ties the collapse to the London journey without giving this day. Berlin is used here because Berlin is where he lived, and the inference is marked rather than hidden. A composer works at a keyboard with two hands. From this morning he has one, and everything written afterward reaches paper through somebody else's fingers, at his dictation, in his son's hand.
suggested_refs: The 5 January 1912 stroke: no city named in the English article, no date given in the German

stops.name: Berlin, the Manifesto of the Ninety-Three
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year only in the sources consulted; the date field defaults to the first of January and does not assert a day. The place is inferred from residence
stops.campa: His name stands among the ninety-three German intellectuals who sign the public declaration defending Germany's conduct in the opening months of the war. Scientists, painters, theologians and composers sign together; the document is answered abroad with contempt and at home with relief. He is a paralysed man of sixty whose life's work is a children's opera, and he signs it. The sources reachable here give the year and not the day, and none of them records what he thought he was signing.

stops.campa: Hedwig Humperdinck dies in the third year of the war. The German article gives the year and nothing else, no day and no city, and Berlin is supplied here because Berlin is where the household was. They had been married twenty-four years, from a spring in Poppelsdorf whose exact date the two Wikipedias still cannot agree on. He survives her by five years, works through them with his right hand and his son's, and will be laid beside her in a grave outside the city.

stops.name: Darmstadt, Gaudeamus finished by another hand
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by German Wikipedia for the Darmstadt premiere. Genre and completion date are contested: English Wikipedia calls Gaudeamus a choral work completed in 1918, German Wikipedia a Spieloper composed 1915-1919. Neither is preferred here
stops.campa: Gaudeamus, scenes from German student life, has its premiere at Darmstadt. English Wikipedia calls it a choral work completed in 1918 with the practical help of his son Wolfram; German Wikipedia calls it a Spieloper composed between 1915 and 1919. The genre and the finishing date do not agree between the two articles and are not reconciled here. What both accounts allow is the working arrangement: the father hears the piece and speaks it, and the son puts it on the paper.

stops.name: Neustrelitz, Der Freischütz at the Landestheater
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day; the opera is corrected here to Weber's Der Freischütz, named independently by both Wikipedias, and Wolfram is described as its stager rather than certainly its conductor
stops.campa: He travels to Neustrelitz in Mecklenburg, where Wolfram is staging Weber's Der Freischütz at the court theatre, and sits in the house for the performance. Weber's is the opera that turned a German forest into a national sound a century before Humperdinck sent two children into one. During the evening he suffers a heart attack. He is sixty-seven, nine years into the paralysis, and he has come the length of the country to watch his son work in a provincial theatre.

stops.name: Neustrelitz, the death
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day and place by both Wikipedias; the nature of the fatal event is contested, English Wikipedia calling it a second heart attack and German Wikipedia a stroke, and the disagreement is reported rather than resolved
stops.campa: He dies the following day at Neustrelitz, aged sixty-seven. English Wikipedia calls the fatal event a second heart attack and German Wikipedia calls it a stroke; the two articles disagree about how he died, and the disagreement is reported here instead of choosing between them. Forty years earlier he had ruled bar lines on Wagner's paper at Wahnfried and expected his life to be spent in that house's shadow. What outlives him is a set of songs a sister asked for one autumn in Frankfurt.

A second memorial stone stands for him at the Zehlendorf cemetery in Berlin, Field 008, some kilometres away from the body, and no source consulted explains why there are two stones for one man. stops.name: Berlin, the State Opera plays it in his memory
stops.date_confidence: reconstruction; English Wikipedia says only that the memorial performance came weeks after the death, and the date here is placed for sequence rather than asserted
stops.campa: Weeks after the funeral the Berlin State Opera gives Hänsel und Gretel in his memory, on the stage where his own comic opera had failed to hold a repertory place sixteen years earlier. The source gives weeks and no date, and the pin here is placed for order alone. It is the start of a pattern that has not stopped since: the opera enters the December calendar of German and Austrian houses as fixed as Advent, and stays there while the rest of the catalogue thins away to nothing.

stops.name: New York, the first opera broadcast complete
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by English Wikipedia; the coordinate is the old Metropolitan Opera House at 1411 Broadway, the company's home in 1931
stops.campa: On Christmas Day the Metropolitan Opera broadcasts Hänsel und Gretel entire on radio, the first complete opera the house has ever put on the air. The technology is new and the choice of work is not accidental. An opera whose tunes a family already sings at home is the one that travels best through a loudspeaker into a room with no stage in it. Twenty-one years before, this same theatre had given his Königskinder its world premiere, and by now almost nobody outside the building remembers that.

stops.name: Schenectady, the first opera on television
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by English Wikipedia
stops.campa: Station WRGB at Schenectady transmits Hänsel und Gretel complete, the first opera ever broadcast on television, fifty years to the day after the Weimar premiere. The war is on and the audience is a few thousand receivers in the Mohawk valley. Each new medium of the century reaches for the same work first, for the same reasons every new theatre did: it is short, its tunes are already in the house, and it happens at Christmas, when the machine that carries it is being demonstrated to families.

stops.campa: A British singer born Arnold George Dorsey takes the dead composer's name for a stage name and becomes famous under it. Within a few years the words Engelbert Humperdinck mean, to most people who hear them anywhere in the English-speaking world, a man with a microphone rather than the man who wrote the evening prayer. The composer left nothing anticipating this. The bare fact of the borrowing is attested; reading it as a fate that befell him is an interpretation, offered here and marked as such.
